items.notes: Document root; original Articles and subsequently ratified amendments. No legal authority is implied by root graph membership.

items.label: Preamble
items.notes: Preamble is not itself catalogued as an independent grant of governmental power.

items.label: Interstate Privileges, Extradition, and Superseded Service Clause
Admission of States and Federal Property
Article VI — Supremacy, Debts, Oaths, and Religious Tests
Taxation, spending and uniformity
items.notes: Congress may levy taxes and provide for common defense/general welfare, subject to qualifications.

items.label: Borrowing
items.notes: Congress may borrow on the credit of the United States.

items.label: Commerce
items.notes: Congress may regulate commerce with foreign nations, among states, and with Indian tribes.

items.label: Naturalization and bankruptcy
items.notes: Congress may establish uniform naturalization rules and bankruptcy laws.

items.label: Coinage and monetary standards
items.notes: Congress may coin money and regulate its value, and fix standards of weights and measures.

items.label: Counterfeiting
items.notes: Congress may provide punishment for counterfeiting federal securities and coin.

items.label: Post offices and roads
items.notes: Congress may establish post offices and post roads.

items.label: Copyrights and patents
items.notes: Congress may secure limited exclusive rights for authors and inventors to promote progress.

items.label: Inferior tribunals
items.notes: Congress may constitute tribunals inferior to the Supreme Court.

items.label: Piracies and offenses against law of nations
items.notes: Congress may define and punish piracies, high-seas felonies, and offenses against the law of nations.

items.label: Declare war, captures and letters of marque
items.notes: Congress may declare war and grant letters of marque and reprisal, with capture rules.

items.label: Armies and appropriation duration
items.notes: Congress may raise and support armies, subject to the two-year appropriation limit.

items.label: Navy
items.notes: Congress may provide and maintain a navy.

items.label: Land and naval forces rules
items.notes: Congress may make rules governing and regulating land and naval forces.

items.label: Call forth militia
items.notes: Congress may provide for calling forth militia for specified purposes.

items.label: Militia organization and reserved state roles
items.notes: Congress may provide for organizing, arming and disciplining militia subject to reserved state functions.

items.label: Federal district and enclaves
items.notes: Congress may exercise specified exclusive legislation over the federal district and acquired places.

items.label: Necessary and Proper laws
items.notes: Congress may enact laws necessary and proper to execute constitutionally vested federal powers.
